chapter: Trumpet players of the old days
title: Joe Johnson, Chip and Tick Chambers
summary: Talk of trumpeters Joe Johnson, Lee Collins's wrestling, Chip, Jesse and Tick Chambers.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, there were a couple of other trumpet players on the front of my mind. Joe Johnson, do you remember him on the trumpet from uptown? Lee Collins used to tell me about it.
Yeah, Lee Collins, he used to play wrestling. He'd go to sleep on Coley. Yeah, Joe Johnson played trumpets up there.
Do you remember Joe Johnson, what he played like, or what style?

No, I can't tell you for long. I remember ragtime, not Chip. Chip was a good trumpet player, favorite kid. I remember Chip. He played bass after, but he was a trumpet player. Chip and a fellow they called Jesse. He used to get all them jobs, guitar players. Jesse.
Oh, and Tick Chambers was another trumpet player.

Yeah, he went to Chicago to go outside tomorrow and Tick Chambers was another trumpet player. He played Kedora Band too. How did he sound? Do you remember? He was a gut bucket trumpet player. The other brother that you should know, Sugar Johnny.
